first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because she's torn between dry season and a December date. It's sensible and calm, no silly slang, and it quotes Smartraveller, which I trust. I read it top to bottom on the iPad. The rain questions near the end are good, especially the one about deposits if we move indoors or change the date. But the middle is heavy going: lists of Indonesian holidays and rainfall in millimetres. And for a page about timing, it says nothing about heat or humidity for older guests, or travel insurance, or who we ring on the day.

journey.quote: There is no single right time to get married in Bali.
journey.reaction: Honest, at least. Nobody's selling me a perfect month. Though I did want someone to tell me which one.

journey.section: What are Bali's dry and wet seasons?
journey.quote: Heavy rain can cause significant flooding in urban areas including Bali, disrupting roads and transport.
journey.reaction: That's the government saying it, not a brochure. It makes me think about Mum stuck in a car for two hours.

journey.quote: It is also a full month of holidays in 2027: Labour Day on 1 May, Ascension Day on 6 May, Idul Adha on 17 May and Waisak on 20 May, with collective leave on 18 and 19 May.
journey.reaction: I don't understand what a holiday there means for us. Is the venue shut? Are flights dearer? It lists the dates but not why I should care.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: A day under 5 mm is very light rain, 5 to 20 mm light, 20 to 50 mm moderate, 50 to 100 mm heavy and over 100 mm very heavy.
journey.reaction: I'm not going to read Indonesian weather bulletins. That's what we'd be paying someone for. I skimmed this whole section.

journey.quote: The 2027 national holidays are 1 and 5 January, 6 February, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 28 March, 1, 6, 17 and 20 May, 1 and 6 June, 15 and 17 August, and 25 and 26 December.
journey.reaction: A wall of numbers. On the iPad my eyes just slid off it.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Notice the capacities. A chapel for 70 and a lawn for 250 suit very different guest lists, and the covered space needs to hold everyone, not only the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the practical point I'd have missed. No use having a lovely chapel if half the family is standing in the rain.

journey.quote: If you move indoors or change the date, how do deposits and payments carry across, and what does the contract say in writing?
journey.reaction: Exactly my question. I'll print this list for Geoff. But it's still us doing the asking. Is the deposit protected if the venue goes under?

journey.quote: Smartraveller notes dengue occurs in Bali and advises rabies vaccination before travel.
journey.reaction: I'd never have thought of rabies. Mum's GP will need to know. But nothing about heat, mobility or medical insurance for older guests.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the covered plan and the weather call are settled before the deposit is paid.
journey.reaction: In writing, before the deposit. That's what I want to hear. Someone accountable.

journey.quote: You move to the covered space agreed in your contract.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, our time zone. Good. I'd still want a name and a phone call, and to know who answers at 2am Bali time.

unanswered_questions: Which months are hottest and most humid, and which suit elderly guests best?
Should older guests have travel insurance with medical cover, and when should it be taken out?
Are our deposits protected if a Bali venue or supplier fails? (deferred business detail)
Who do we ring if something goes wrong in Bali after hours, and is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there on the day? (deferred business detail)
What does a public holiday actually change for a wedding: venue staffing, flight prices, traffic?
Do any of these chapels have step-free access for someone with a walking frame?
Roughly what does a Bali wedding cost in dry versus wet season, From AUD?
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join as a parent paying part?

turn_offs_found.quote: The 2027 national holidays are 1 and 5 January, 6 February, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 28 March, 1, 6, 17 and 20 May, 1 and 6 June, 15 and 17 August, and 25 and 26 December.
turn_offs_found.why: A long unbroken run of dates. My card's turn-off is long unbroken paragraphs; a small table would be far easier on the iPad.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you move indoors or change the date, how do deposits and payments carry across, and what does the contract say in writing?
turn_offs_found.why: Right question, but it leaves the asking to us. The page never says who is responsible for our money or whether deposits are protected.

would_share_with: My husband, the 'Questions to ask your venue' list and the closing paragraph about AUD quotes and one point of contact
My mother, the dengue and rabies line so she can talk to her GP
My daughter, the line about the covered space needing to hold everyone, before she falls for a chapel for 70

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
cta_reaction.why: The right words, and the 'in writing before the deposit' line helps. I'd talk to Geoff first, then want a phone call with a real person about deposit protection, insurance and who we ring on the day.

top_3_changes: Add a sourced line on heat and humidity by season, and a note that older guests should check medical travel insurance, with the 'when' tied to the first deposit; flag if not sourceable.
Turn the 2027 holiday paragraph into a short table and say in one line what a holiday means for a wedding (staffing, traffic, flights), sourced or flagged.
Next to the deposits question, say what Wedded Concierge does about deposits and on-the-day contact in Bali, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, accountability, elderly guests, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; deposit protection, on-the-day contact, pricing and insurance placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the business confirm what Wedded Concierge does about deposits and on-the-day contact in Bali, and is there a source for heat/humidity and insurance guidance for older guests? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half.
Relevance and enquiry are 3 because the post is mainly a weather and holiday calendar guide; the venue questions and closing section lift trust to 4.
Husband's name (Geoff) is character colour consistent with earlier panels, not a page fact.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom, BMKG and holiday-list sections skimmed as she would.
